articles.headline: Our Camden Letter. Deferred Correspondence (the Camden riot of Sept. 9, 1864)
articles.author: West Jersey
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Our readers have doubtless been waiting to hear something of the recent troubles in our town, about which there has been many conflicting reports, which, for the most part, are wilful misrepresentations circulated for political purposes. ... The first one of these re-unions came off in Camden, on Friday, the 9th inst. Our readers have doubtless heard it spoken of as the negro riot. Dated Camden, September 10th, 1864.

articles.headline: Letter from the Front (Chaplain H. M. Turner described)
articles.summary: In the Field near Petersburg, Va., Sept. 1st, 1864. Mr. Weaver: Dear Sir, I have read closely your paper for a long time, but would not obtrude an article until now. ... Grant, colored soldiers, bounties offered to contrabands to go as substitutes, storms in camp, and an interview with Rev. H. M. Turner, Chaplain 1st U.S.C. Troops. Non-Philadelphia; signer not read.

articles.headline: A Letter to the Bishops of the A.M.E. Church and Superintendents of the Z.A.M.E. Churches
articles.author: Henry M. Turner
articles.summary: Headquarters 1st U.S.C.T., Harrison's Landing, Va., September 21, 1864. I hope it will not be considered presumptive or sacrilegious for a poor soldier upon the field of battle to solicit your grave attention a few moments. ... Warns that M.E. Church chaplains are seizing colored churches in captured Southern cities. Signed Henry M. Turner, Chaplain 1st U.S.C.T. (Baltimore Conference; text only).

articles.headline: From near Petersburg, Va.
articles.author: James H. Payne
articles.summary: Camp near Petersburg, Va., September 19th, 1864. Mr. Editor: Permit me the privilege of saying a few words of encouragement, through the columns of your paper, to the A.M.E. Church. Signed James H. Payne, Quartermaster-Serg't 27th U.S.C.T. (non-Philadelphia; text only).

articles.headline: Report of the Proceedings of the Second General Conference of the B.M.E. Church (Chatham, C.W.)
articles.author: W. H. Jones [VERIFY]
articles.summary: The Second General Conference of the B.M.E. Church in Canada commenced its deliberations in the Victoria Chapel, Princess Street, Chatham, C.W., on the 5th of September, 1864, at the hour of 9 o'clock, Right Rev. Willis Nazrey presiding. Rev. John M. Brown appeared as chairman of the delegation from the A.M.E. General Conference. Canadian; text only except the bishops.
people: presiding bishop, B.M.E. General Conference (Right Rev.)

articles.headline: Norfolk Correspondence
articles.author: John Oliver
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Thinking it might be interesting to you and the numerous readers of the Recorder, to know something of the condition of the colored people in this vicinity, and matters connected with them, I submit the following. Freedpeople's farms, slab-towns, schools, mission houses at Norfolk and Portsmouth. Signed John Oliver.

articles.headline: Cambridge, Mass., meeting to send delegates to the Syracuse National Convention
articles.author: A. M. H.
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Sir: Heretofore, the citizens of this place have acted in conjunction with our friends in Boston, on all matters of public interest, in consequence of being so few in number. ... In answer to the call of the Committee, for a National Convention, to be held at Syracuse, N.Y., on the 4th of Oct., 1864, our citizens held a large and enthusiastic meeting, in Stearns' Chapel, Harvard St., on Friday evening, Sept. 16th. Nelson L. Perkins president; delegates chosen included William Wells Brown. Dated Cambridge, September 17th, 1864. Non-Philadelphia; text only.

articles.headline: New Arrangements for Correspondents; price notice
articles.summary: All who write for the Christian Recorder will hereafter please address as follows: 'Christian Recorder, Box No. 2975, Philadelphia, Pa.' All who wish to address the editor personally will please direct: 'Rev. Elisha Weaver, Box 2975, Philadelphia, Pa.' Price two dollars and a half a year if paid in advance, three dollars if not.

articles.headline: Appointments for the Union A.M.E. Church, Coates St., Philadelphia
articles.author: A. L. Stanford
articles.summary: On Sabbath, the 2d of October, at 3 o'clock P.M., a sermon will be delivered for the benefit of the Sabbath School. Subject: 'Passing through the fire to Moloch.' A sermon will be delivered in the evening at 7 1/2 o'clock. ... On Sabbath, the 16th of October, there will be Quarterly Meeting held. A. L. Stanford, Minister.

articles.headline: Evening Schools (Friends)
articles.summary: The Friends will open their Schools for colored Men and Women, on Monday evening next, October 3d, at the corner of Raspberry and Aurora streets. They desire their colored friends to turn out in full force. Instruction free. Open five evenings in the week, from 7 to 9 o'clock.

articles.headline: Quarterly Meetings, Macedonia and Deep Cut (N.J.)
articles.author: T. G. Steward
articles.summary: Our second course of Quarterly Meetings will commence October 9th, at Macedonia; October 16th, at Deep Cut. Quarterly Conference, Friday evening, October 7th. T. G. Steward, Pastor. Rev. Wm. Moore, Elder.

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting, Mount Zion A.M.E. Church, Trenton, N.J.
articles.author: Thomas H. Cooper
articles.summary: A Quarterly Meeting will be held in the A.M.E. Mount Zion Church, Trenton, N.J., on the first Sabbath in October, 1864. Love Feast will take place in the morning. Doors open at 9 1/2 o'clock, a.m. ... preaching at 10 1/2 a.m., 3, and 7 1/2 p.m. All are invited. Thomas H. Cooper, Minister.

articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: Sunday, Oct. 2d, 10 o'clock, Frankford, Pa. Sunday night, Oct. 2d, 7 1/2 P.M., Camden, N.J. Monday night, Oct. 3d, Chester, Pa. A. W. Wayman.

articles.headline: Thornbury Quarterly Meeting
articles.summary: Quarterly Meeting will be held at Thornbury, Oct. 15, at 3 o'clock.

articles.headline: Colored People and the War. A Visit to Camp Wm. Penn
articles.summary: On last Monday morning we paid a visit to Camp William Penn, in company with two ladies from Allegheny City, who are esteemed members of Rev. Samuel Watt's congregation. The husbands of both these ladies are at the present time in the service of 'Uncle Sam.' ... We also had the pleasure while there of meeting with our old and much esteemed friend, Mr William Sill, who is acting in the capacity of post-sutler.
people: post-sutler at Camp William Penn (printed 'Sill'; see notes)

articles.headline: The National Convention of Colored Men (Syracuse)
articles.summary: To be held at Syracuse, N.Y., on the 4th instant. We find that there will be a strong representation throughout the country at this Convention. ... urges unity, securing full rights as freemen, and that our people should become a business-doing class. 'The people will be better judges when they shall have seen the conclusions to which this Convention will arrive.'

articles.headline: Departure of Colored Troops for the Field (127th U.S.C.T.)
articles.summary: The 127th Regiment of United States Colored Troops took their departure for the field of battle on last Wednesday. Leaving their late camping ground, known by the name of Camp William Penn, ... they marched down Chestnut street to headquarters ... to the Union and Cooper Volunteer Refreshment Saloons. ... This is the ninth regiment that has left Camp William Penn, and the tenth is already more than half full.

articles.headline: Great Effort on the Part of Bethel and Wesley Churches
articles.summary: On last Sabbath morning we visited Bethel church, and had the pleasure of hearing Rev. Joseph Smith preach. ... A most generous collection was taken up in this church, amounting to about one hundred and twenty-five dollars during the day. We understand that Wesley church made strenuous efforts towards the same object.

articles.headline: Assault on Sergeant-Major Green (Colored)
articles.summary: A few days ago, as Sergeant Major Green, of the One Hundred and Twenty-seventh United States Colored Troops, was quietly passing along South Street, he was assailed by a number of ruffians without any provocation whatever. ... The Major then pulled his pistol out of his pocket and beat them over the head with the butt end of it. They then tried stones, when he fired, shooting one of the assailants. ... trial before Alderman Carter ... On last Wednesday, Sergeant-Major Greene was admitted to bail.

articles.headline: Festival at the Union Baptist Church
articles.summary: A grand Festival entertainment was held, last Wednesday and Thursday, at the Union Baptist Church, under the pastoral care of Rev. Mr. Hamilton. The good ladies of the church spared no pains to have every thing in the best style.

articles.headline: Our Friend, Mr. Brown, in Fifth Street, above Walnut (puff)
articles.summary: The above named gentleman attends promptly to all work in his line of business, such as cleaning and repairing gentlemen's clothing. He is recommended by all who have had business transactions with him.

articles.headline: Bought Out (Continental eating saloon, Lombard street)
articles.summary: It will be seen that Mr. Charles W. Brister has purchased Mr. Cole's Eating Saloon, in Lombard street, under the old Institute. We dropped in there a day or two ago, and found that he had made considerable improvement. ... Those who want a good dish of oysters, or any thing else in the eating line, can be accommodated.
people: purchaser and proprietor, eating saloon, Lombard St. under the old Institute

articles.headline: Rev. Stephen Smith
articles.summary: Of Philadelphia, has been quite indisposed. We are glad to announce to his friends that he is much better, and has not gone to his final resting-place yet, as some of his friends, it seems, have heard, and written him on the same subject.

articles.headline: Brooklyn Correspondence (Syracuse delegates)
articles.summary: Questions of the Day; National Convention assembles at Syracuse, Oct. 4th. New York and Brooklyn have chosen delegates and are holding weekly meetings. Non-Philadelphia; text only.

articles.headline: Camden Correspondence (reply to 'Wild Jack')
articles.author: Thomas L. Brown
articles.summary: 'Why strive ye, one with another,' said Moses to the children of Israel, 'seeing that ye are brethren?' Mr. Editor, It is certainly strange that, in these days of light and literature, there can be found men who are willing to spend their time ... Defends the 54th and 55th Mass. regiments against 'Wild Jack' and G. H. White. Dated Camden, N.J., Sept 25th, 1864.

articles.headline: An Interesting Dialogue
articles.author: Edward J. W... [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I had an interview with a gentleman on the morning of the 22d, while waiting for the cars. 'Good morning, sergeant,' said he. ... 'I belong to the Fourth Regiment United States Colored Troops, sir.' Dated Philadelphia, Sept 23, 1864; the writer, a Baltimore-born sergeant of the 4th U.S.C.T. Text only.

articles.headline: Olive Branch Boarding House (new address)
articles.summary: Olive Branch Boarding House, No. 814 Lombard Street, Phila. Mrs. H. M. Cropper respectfully announces to Travellers that she has opened a first-class Boarding House for their special accommodation, in a central (to business or churches) part of the city.
people: proprietor, Olive Branch Boarding House, No. 814 [VERIFY] Lombard St. (Mrs.)

articles.headline: Army Correspondence, by Chaplain Turner
articles.author: H. M. T.
articles.summary: Head Quarters 1st U.S. Troops, Harrison's Landing, Va., Sept. 28, 1864. Mr. Editor: The change of scenes which are so singularly and significantly revolutionizing other localities, are not wanting in the place we now occupy. Revival in the regiment; new chaplains' uniform order; the soldiers' clamor for spelling-books. Text only.

articles.headline: Items by the Way (Cincinnati to Cleveland, Oberlin, Keokuk)
articles.author: Mabella [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Ill health and a change in my base of operations prevented me from fulfilling my promise, viz: to write you once more from the Queen City. ... Oberlin commencement (J. H. Cook of Detroit the only colored graduate), Cleveland Sabbath-school under Elder Warren. Dated Keokuk, Iowa, Sept. 14, 1864. Non-Philadelphia; text only.

articles.headline: The Present Crisis
articles.author: Anata R. Demby [VERIFY]
articles.summary: What should the colored race do in the present crisis? is a question that forces itself upon the mind of every thinking man and woman. Should we meekly submit to the threats, insults, and bruises that have been heaped upon our ancestors, and upon ourselves for so long a period ...? Dated Philadelphia, Sept. 27th, 1864.

articles.headline: A Sermon to the Sabbath School (Union A.M.E. Sabbath School)
articles.author: A. B.
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: You will please excuse us for intruding upon your columns so soon again. We did not think when we troubled you about Bishop Campbell visiting our school, that we would be compelled, by our impulse, to trouble you so soon again ... On last Sabbath our pastor, Rev. A. L. Stanford, preached a special discourse to the Sabbath-school children of our church. Dated Philadelphia, Oct. 3d, 1864. (Also named, reading uncertain: Angelina H. Demby [VERIFY] (essayist, 'Mental and moral culture' (Miss)).)
people: speaker, just returned from the B.M.E. Conference

articles.headline: Our Norfolk Correspondence. The Wounded Colored Soldiers
articles.author: Sallie
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: About half-past seven o'clock this morning information reached us that the steamer George Washington had arrived at Portsmouth from the front, having a large number of the wounded colored soldiers on board, among whom was Sergt. Major T. R. Hawkins, of the 6th U.S.C.T. ... Sergeant H. is dreadfully wounded in three places: the shoulder, thigh, and foot. ... Miss M. C. Highgate left for Syracuse, N.Y.; Capt. J. Brown and Prof. W. H. Woodbury named superintendents of colored schools.

articles.headline: Florida Correspondence
articles.author: R. M. Smith
articles.summary: Jacksonville, Florida, Sept. 18, 1864. Mr. Editor: My time being leisurely spent the earlier part of the day, I thought that I would indite a few lines for your valuable paper, that the people of the North may know that the United States Colored Troops are still striving to crush and annihilate this unholy rebellion. ... the 'Bloody Third'. Signed R. M. Smith, Drummer, Co. A, 3d U.S.C.T.

articles.headline: Bishop Wayman's Appointments for October, 1864
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: Sabbath, October 9th, Cumberland, Md. ... Sabbath morning, October 30th, Thornbury, Penna. Sabbath afternoon, October 30th, Westtown, Penna. Sabbath night, October 30th, West Chester, Penna. Tuesday night, October 31, Media, Pa. Wednesday night, November 1st, Unionville, Penna. Thursday night, November 2d, Oxford, Pennsylvania. ... We also called the attention of the Philadelphia Conference to Rev. J. G. Bulaugh. He is quite feeble in health. Brethren, do not forget your obligation to him. A. W. W.
people: Philadelphia Conference minister, in feeble health (Rev.)

articles.headline: To the Ministers of the Philadelphia and New York Conferences (subscription appeal)
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: Dear Brethren: The Editor of the Christian Recorder is making great efforts to increase the number of subscribers to ten thousand; and as the other Conferences have pledged themselves to raise their part, we ask you to put forth some exertion to raise your part. Also: postage notice; to any town in Philadelphia County the Recorder goes free.

articles.headline: The Late Special Collection at Bethel Church
articles.summary: Last week, we noticed that a collection was taken up at the above-named church. We have been kindly furnished with the different items by Mr. Custis, a well-known and gentlemanly Trustee of the church. They are as follows: Rev. Wm. Moore $1.00 [VERIFY]; Trustees of the church $7.00; Stewards and Class leaders $25.00; Congregation $81.25 [VERIFY]; the church choir $0.75; L. R. Seymour, Secretary of Trustees, $1.00. Total amount, $125.00.

articles.headline: A Word to the Wise is Sufficient (to correspondents)
articles.summary: But how many words are absolutely necessary to the unwise? We cannot say. Under this caption we desire to say a few words to some of our correspondents; not to all, but to a worthy few.

articles.headline: The War and its Design
articles.author: J. P. C.
articles.summary: That war is an evil, every body believes and nobody denies. ... God has permitted, yea, sent the present war upon us because this nation had sinned against Him. ... Let the oppressor do justice to the slave and his descendants, and peace will be proclaimed within ninety days.

articles.headline: Rev. John M. Brown
articles.summary: This worthy brother, who is stationed at Norfolk, left our city on Tuesday, en route for home. He has been visiting the B.M.E. General Conference, to which he was appointed a delegate by the A.M.E. General Conference, which met in our city in last May.
people: Rev.; A.M.E. delegate to B.M.E. General Conference

articles.headline: Shall We Sustain the Government?
articles.author: Charles W. Strother [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Defences of Louisville, Ky., September 18th, 1864. Mr. Editor: It is with feelings known only by those who are true to the cause of freedom, that I address you these few lines. Signed Sergt. Co. A, 107th U.S.C.T. Non-Philadelphia; text only.

articles.author: Jonathan Hamilton [VERIFY]
articles.summary: New Haven, September 29, 1864. Dear Bro. Weaver: It is not often that I trouble the columns of the Christian Recorder. ... my much esteemed brother, William H. Ross, lying very low ... revival under Elder Grimes. Non-Philadelphia; text only.

articles.headline: Our Delegates to the National Convention
articles.author: Charles B. Colly
articles.summary: At a meeting of the colored citizens of Philadelphia, held at the Philadelphia Institute, on Saturday evening, October 1st, 1864, the Rev. Jonathan C. Gibbs was appointed chairman, and Charles H. Colley, secretary. The object of the meeting, to elect delegates to represent them in the National Convention of colored men, to be held in the city of Syracuse, on Tuesday, the 4th inst., was briefly stated by Prof. E. articles.headline: A Soldier's Idea of What Those at Home Should Do
articles.author: Wm. H. Davis
articles.summary: Camp in the Field, Crow's Nest, Va., September 24th, 1864. Mr. Editor: Dear Sir: I have been asked several times since I have been in the army why I did not correspond with your valuable paper ... I thought of what had been done for them that so many of her noble sons should enlist in the service of the United States, and thus counted in the quota of Pennsylvania. ... I am aware that you are going to hold a State Convention, but for what purpose I do not know, unless it be for toleration in the cars running to and fro through your city. I recommend you to get your franchise acknowledged first. Signed Wm. H. Davis, Band-Master 22d Regiment United States Col. Troops.

articles.headline: Letter from the 22d U.S.C.T. (Crow's Nest, Dutch Gap canal)
articles.author: Charles A. Haitsrock [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Dear Editor: I, for the first time, attempt to address you with these few lines. I have been a servant of Uncle Samuel's for nearly a year ... Our regiment is now lying near the James River, at a place called Crow's Nest. Signed Orderly Sergt. Co. H, 22d U.S.C.T., Fortress Monroe, Va., Sept. 26th, 1864. Camp William Penn regiment.

articles.headline: Army Correspondence (3d U.S.C.T., Yellow Bluff, Fla.)
articles.author: Thomas B. Rockhold [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Headquarters 3d U.S.C.T., Camp Jacksonville, Florida, September 16, 1864. My Dear Brother Weaver: In noticing some of your later papers of last month, I saw my name in one of them as writer of a piece to be published in your paper. ... Our chaplain ... His name is Hobbs, of Lancaster City, Pennsylvania ... Company D, 3d U.S.C.T., now stationed at Yellow Bluff, commanded by Captain John L. Bruor ... muster 60 men out of 81 that we had when we left Camp William Penn. Signed Orderly-Sergeant Co. D, 3d U.S.C.T.

articles.headline: Brooklyn, New York (concert; Syracuse convention)
articles.author: G. W. H.
articles.summary: Brooklyn: The Literary, Musical Concert and Exhibition; The War; Politics; Colored National Convention. Non-Philadelphia; text only.

articles.summary: Wilberforce University. Mr. Editor: Sir: Thinking that you would like to hear from this part of the country, I embrace the present opportunity to inform you, that the students of the Institution met in the chapel ... for the purpose of organizing a Society. Ohio; text only.

articles.headline: Ten Thousand Subscribers (editorial)
articles.summary: We shall not forget to keep before the minds of the people and our ministers the great importance of their untiring efforts to procure the ten thousand cash subscribers ... We are glad that Bishop Wayman has called the attention of the Philadelphia brethren to our call.

articles.headline: National Convention of Colored Men in America (editor's report)
articles.summary: We left Philadelphia in company with the delegates from our city for the National Convention, which was appointed to meet in Syracuse, N.Y. We arrived in New York a little after 2 o'clock, P.M., and remained in the city until 6 o'clock, P.M., at which time we took the finest boat we were ever on, for the city of Albany ... The Convention established a Bureau, having its headquarters in the city of Philadelphia, Pa. Mr. John Langston, Esq., was elected Chairman, and Rev. John Peck, of Pittsburg, was appointed as first Vice-President. Mr. Turner, of Philadelphia, was made the Secretary of this great Union League Company of the colored citizens of the United States.
people: of Philadelphia, teaching the freedmen at Norfolk (Miss)

articles.headline: The Election (Pennsylvania, Oct. 11)
articles.summary: On last Tuesday the Election was held throughout the entire State of Pennsylvania, and, as far as we could learn, up to the time of going to press, the Republican party had triumphed, and Copperheadism was at a discount. Our much esteemed friend, the Hon. Mr. Kelly, of the U.S. Congress ... has run far before his political opponent.

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting at Westtown
articles.summary: On last Sabbath we held quarterly meeting for Brother Laws, at Westtown, and we had a good time of it, both at the Quarterly Conference and at public worship. ... To-day we hold quarterly meeting for Brother Cornish at Horntown [VERIFY]. Surname-only ministers not linked.

articles.headline: New Virginia House (Mrs. Rebecca Mason, Norfolk)
articles.summary: Mrs Rebecca Mason respectfully announces to travellers, that she has opened a house at No. 7 Union Street, Norfolk, for their accommodation, and which she hopes to make a true Virginian home. Norfolk; text only.

articles.headline: Card of thanks for a surprise party
articles.author: W. H. W. Winder

Mr. Albert Stevens presented me a box, containing some eight dollars ... The Committee were: Mrs. Butler, Mrs. Elizabeth Artes, and Miss Jemima Jones. Dated Philadelphia, Oct. 10, 1864.

articles.author: West Jersey
articles.summary: The Christian Recorder: its claims; it must be supported; its moral and religious worth; its contributors; Macedonia Church quarterly meeting; the collection for the minister. ... Elder Stanford held forth in the morning, after Love-feast ... Bishop Campbell filled the 3 P.M. appointment ... In the evening, the congregation was entertained by the pastor, T. G. Steward. ... The collection, all day, amounted to something over $30. Dated Camden, N.J., October, 1864.

articles.headline: Bishop Wayman's Visits during September
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: On Sunday, September 4th, we commenced our visits for the past month. Ellicott's Mills, Maryland was the first place we went to. ... Washington (Bible presented to President Lincoln by the colored people of Baltimore) ... Annapolis, York, Wrightsville, Columbia, Marietta, Lancaster, Mount Joy, Pottsville, Reading, Norristown, Deep Valley ... Sunday morning, the 18th, ... I turned in at Bethel, and found Brother Moore's people all right. Sunday afternoon we spent at Mount Pisgah, West Philadelphia ... At night, we wandered up to Zion Mission Church, Brother Winder's charge. ... Gouldtown, Bridgeton, Springtown (Brother Woodlin), Salem (Brother Long), Bushtown and Woodbury (Brother Berney [VERIFY]), Snow Hill (Brother Henry [VERIFY]). Dated Baltimore, Oct. 4th, 1864.

articles.author: Lewis Buchanan
articles.summary: [Opening on the missing page 2.] ...There are two colored regiments here besides ours, and they are regiments that have proved themselves to be fighting men. General Asboth, about two weeks ago, had a fight, defeated and captured some Johnnies and brought from them some three or four hundred of our people... articles.author: Jno. C. Brock [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Camp near Petersburg, Va., Oct. [?], 1864. Dear Recorder:--Since the last letter I wrote to you, we have been engaged with the enemy. On last Tuesday we were ordered to take six days' rations... In our regiment (the 43rd) we had [officers and] several men killed... The colored soldiers of the 9th Corps, together with their heroic companions of the 18th Corps, have well established the reputation of our soldierly abilities. Signed Com. Sergt., 43rd U.S.C.V.

Vols., Folly Island, S.C., October 14th, 1864. Mr. Editor:--Doubtless you will have heard before this reaches you, that the Fifty-fourth and Fifty-fifth Massachusetts regiments have been paid... Our splendid Regimental Band played a number of popular airs... Mr. John Moore, of Philadelphia, its accomplished leader, deserves all praise.

articles.headline: Letter from a Soldier (25th U.S.C.T., Fort Pickens, Fla.)
articles.author: James S. Johnson [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Fort Pickens, Fla., October 20, 1864. Mr. Editor.--Sir:--It being my first effort at correspondence I am in hopes that you will excuse this feeble attempt and insert these few lines in your paper, in behalf of friends and well-wishers of the 25th U.S.C. Infantry, both here and at home. We have had a hard time of it ever since our embarkation from Philadelphia, what with excessive fatigue, scorbutic diseases and fevers... we must wait until next pay-day, which will make us eight months without one cent of pay.

articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: The Book Committee will please take notice that they are especially requested to meet in Bethel church, in the preacher's study, on next Thursday, the 17th instant, at the hour of two o'clock. articles.headline: Notice: grand rally at Bethel on Thanksgiving Day for the Christian Recorder
articles.summary: We take the present opportunity of notifying the members and friends of Bethel Church that there will be a grand rally in that church on Thanksgiving Day, at the hour of ten o'clock, precisely. The pastor, Rev. William Moore, will, with Divine permission, deliver one of his well-known interesting discourses... At the conclusion of the sermon, the claims of the Christian Recorder will be set forth, and a liberal collection taken up. At night there will be a [?] united effort made toward the said named object.

articles.headline: The Conquest (editorial on the election)
articles.summary: The Election is over. The enemies of our country and of liberty, together with the emissaries and coadjutors of 'old Jeff,' have been most signally defeated and overwhelmed, while our glorious emblem of freedom, the banner of freedom, still floats unsullied in the breeze, proclaiming that, at least for 'four years more,' Americans shall rule America! ...the Union candidates--Lincoln, of Illinois, and Johnson, of Tennessee--are placed at the head of the nation... The vote of our heroic soldiers also shows how true the cry is that none but Democrats have gone to war.

articles.headline: Still Another: Dr. Longfellow, of Philadelphia (editorial puff)
articles.summary: This gentleman, a true and working friend, is too well known in the community to need any recommendation that we could possibly give. The Doctor is a firm friend and advocate of the Recorder, and has proved himself such since we have been the Editor;--ever true, faithful and untiring. While in this connection, we would call the attention of our numerous readers to the able article from the pen of this gentleman... [he] proposes to set apart a fixed day for accomplishing the task as a day of thanksgiving and free-will offering.

articles.headline: A Great Work Before Us (editorial: petition the Legislature, colored suffrage in Pennsylvania)
articles.summary: There is now a great work before us. The colored people of Pennsylvania and the friends of freedom within her bounds are very different from those of old Massachusetts, New York, Rhode Island, and some of the other States--that is, the treatment which they receive constitutes the difference. Here we are denied the right of franchise... We should be prepared to present a petition... asking the Legislature to... erase from her statute-book all odious and unreasonable laws... We hope that the Union Leagues of Philadelphia and of the entire State will join with us.

articles.headline: The Bethel Sunday-School, Sixth Street, Philadelphia (editorial)
articles.summary: This is the mother church of the A.M.E. Church, and it is a fact, that it is as large, if not the largest church in the connection, and probably has the largest congregation of orthodox faith. It has also one of the best Superintendents, in the person of Lewis L. Seymour, who is as faithful as one can be in attendance. But, for all this, we are sorry to say, that the number of children, who regularly attend the Sabbath-school, is not what it might be.

articles.headline: A Great Work to be Done (editorial)
articles.summary: Let us again earnestly invite the attention of our brethren to a subject of vast and impending moment. ... There is yet a great and important work to be done by every colored man and woman in this and every other State where we are deprived of the right of franchise, and even riding in the city cars. ... that we may be enabled to induce the repeal of those tyrannical and oppressive black laws which now blot the fair escutcheon of Pennsylvania.

articles.headline: Personal (John M. Langston in the city)

The Union A.M.E. Church, Coates street, was neither forgetful nor neglectful of her duty. articles.headline: Lecture on Thursday night, at Concert Hall, by Theodore Tilton, Esq.
articles.summary: It was formally announced in the papers that Theodore Tilton would deliver one of the course of lectures for the winter in our city. ... Mr. Tilton spoke of the rights of colored men and of equality in treatment. He also made reference to our own city of brotherly love, and of her not allowing colored people to ride in the street cars within her limits; but New York city, discreditably as she has acted in various other ways, makes no distinction as to color in those who ride in her cars. articles.headline: Letter from the Front (43d U.S.C.T., camp between Richmond and Petersburg)
articles.author: James H. Harmon
articles.summary: I seat myself, for the first time, to write a few lines to be published in your paper. I, having enlisted as a private in the 43d Regiment U.S.C.T., on the 14th day of March last, was promoted to 2d Sergeant of Co. C, of which the Rev. John R. V. Morgan is Orderly Sergeant. ... I remained at Camp William Penn until the 11th of July. ... I thank God that he has spared my life so far, and still hope to see the city of brotherly love once more. Signed James H. Harmon, Quarter-master Sergeant of the 43d Regiment U.S.C.T. (Also named, reading uncertain: John C. Hruck [VERIFY] (Commissary Sergeant, 43d U.S.C.T.).)

Davis. ... he concluded that he would enlist. ... appointed Orderly Sergeant of Co. B, 25th Reg't. The circumstance of the passenger railway being closed against the people of color, and the right to vote, are two important subjects to discuss. ... The object for which we have met is to place in the hands of the agent, Rev. E. Weaver, sufficient funds to put the Christian Recorder on a sure foundation ... events.name: Camden, N.J., 'negro riot' (copperhead mob attack)
events.location: Camden, N.J.; vicinity of Third and Spruce Sts.; Locust St.; Spruce St.
events.description: Letter signed 'West Jersey', Camden, Sept 10. About eight o'clock on Friday evening, Sept 9, two or three drunken 'copperheads' near Third and Spruce Sts. picked a quarrel with a woman selling hot corn, then chased a little boy into the house of Mrs. Rosanna [VERIFY] Barnes ('a quiet and peaceable lady, living on Locust St.'), threw her to the floor and surrounded the boy in the yard, until a lady of the same house, Mrs. Chance [VERIFY], drove them off with a tea-kettle of cold water. Police lodged the boy in the lock-up. The mob grew to hundreds with cries of 'kill the niggers, burn 'em out'; about ten or twelve colored men and boys gathered on Spruce St., joined by about two dozen residents (35 or 40 in all); bricks were thrown and one or two shots fired from an alley in self-defense; the fire-bell was rung to 'put down the negroes'. The Republican mayor joined in hunting Black residents; colored men were arrested and fined while the white rioters went free. Writer contrasts this with Crispus Attucks and 125,000 Black soldiers.

events.name: Assault on Sergeant-Major Green, 127th U.S.C.T., South Street
events.location: South Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Sergeant-Major Green (Greene) of the 127th U.S.C.T., in uniform, was assailed without provocation by a gang of ruffians on South Street; he beat them with his pistol butt and, when they threw stones, fired, wounding one, who was taken to the William Penn Hospital. A police officer arrested the sergeant, who offered no resistance; some assailants were also arrested and tried before Alderman Carter, who committed them and the sergeant. Green was admitted to bail on Wednesday. Surname only; not linked. Street violence, not on the cars.

Seth, Julia A. Bruce [VERIFY], Susan A. H. Morris, Caroline V. Still, Fanny Camp, Mary L. Davis, Lucretia Miller, Margaret H. Jones, Cecilia M. Davis and Margaret Jones. Commencement held in Concert Hall with free tickets; essay 'Our Alma Mater' by Octavius V. Catto, teacher. The $5,000 promised by the executors of the estate of Josiah Dawson, deceased, toward a building fund has been obtained; a lot 77 by 125 feet on Shippen street west of Ninth, fronting Ronaldson's Cemetery, purchased; an anonymous Friend offers $5,000 more if $15,000 is raised within a year.

events.name: Philadelphia meeting elects delegates to the National Convention of Colored Men (Syracuse)
events.location: Philadelphia Institute, Philadelphia
events.description: Meeting of the colored citizens of Philadelphia, Saturday evening, October 1st, 1864. Chairman Rev. Jonathan C. Gibbs; secretary Charles H. Colley (signed Charles B. Colly). Prof. E. D. Bassett stated the object. Ten delegates resolved; nominating committee O. V. Catto, D. D. Turner and James C. Glascow [VERIFY]. Delegates elected unanimously: Prof. E. D. Bassett, Alfred M. Green, Rev. Elisha Weaver, D. D. Turner, Rev. John B. Reeve, Dr. H. B. Brown [VERIFY], St. George R. Taylor, Thomas J. Bowers, Rev. Jonathan C. Gibbs and George W. Gaines. Finance committee to defray the delegation's expenses: Lewis R. Seymour, Jesse E. Glascow [VERIFY] and William Riley. The president and secretary were empowered to issue credentials to other gentlemen going to the Convention who would represent the city creditably.

events.name: National Convention of Colored Men, Syracuse: Philadelphia delegation and the National Equal Rights League
events.location: Syracuse, N.Y.
events.description: Editor Weaver's account: he travelled with the Philadelphia delegates via New York (steamboat to Albany, treated 'as white men have always been treated') and Albany (overcharged at an eating saloon), arriving in Syracuse about 2 P.M.; lodged first with a Mr. Lisoard [VERIFY], then, through Rev. J. W. Loguen, at the house of Mr. De Forest with Rev. Mr. Gibbs, Rev. Mr. Reeves (John B. Reeve) and Professor Bassett. Met the editor of the Colored Citizen, Mr. Sampson, John Langston, Esq., Rev. John Peck of Pittsburg, Professor Vashon, Mrs. Ellen Watkins Harper, Miss Edmonia G. Highgate (back from teaching freedmen at Norfolk) and Miss C. C. Duncan, who had left Miss Sallie Daffin of Philadelphia teaching at Norfolk. Resolutions on the rights of the colored man and on forming a compact and permanent union; addresses to be sent to the President and Congress; compliments to Charles Sumner and Gen. Butler; evening audiences never under 2,000. The Convention established a Bureau headquartered in Philadelphia (the league): John Langston, Esq., Chairman; Rev. John Peck of Pittsburg, first Vice-President; 'Mr. Turner, of Philadelphia' (presumably D. D. Turner) Secretary of 'this great Union League Company of the colored citizens of the United States'.

events.name: Coates St. (Union A.M.E.) Sabbath School monthly exercises
events.location: Union A.M.E. Church, Coates St., Philadelphia
events.description: Sunday afternoon exercises (dated by the writer's Oct 5 letter as 'last Sunday', Oct 2): New Testament chapter recited; essays by Miss Angeline R. Demby ('The mental and moral training of children') and Miss Mary S. Thompson ('The advantages of the Sabbath-school'); catechising from the Child's Question Book. Present: Rev. John M. Brown and Dr. Armstrong. At three o'clock Rev. A. L. Stanford preached on 'Passing through the fire to Moloch' (Lev. 18:21). The Union Sunday-school is under superintendent Mr. Andrew Berris [VERIFY]. Reported by Wm. Thos. Simpson. Same occasion as the Oct 8 'A. B.' letter.

events.name: Surprise party for W. H. W. Winder
events.location: Philadelphia
events.description: Young ladies and gentlemen surprised W. H. W. Winder (probably the pastor of Zion Mission; see Wayman's report) about 9 P.M. Oct 5 singing 'Soldiers of Christ, arise'; Mr. Albert Stevens presented a box with some eight dollars. Committee: Mrs. Butler, Mrs. Elizabeth Artes [VERIFY], Miss Jemima Jones.

events.name: Bishop Wayman's Philadelphia visits: Bethel, Mount Pisgah (West Philadelphia), Zion Mission
events.location: Bethel A.M.E.; Mount Pisgah, West Philadelphia; Zion Mission Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Bishop A. W. Wayman, finding there would hardly be a congregation at Germantown on Sunday morning Sept 18, went to Bethel and found Brother Moore's people all right; Sunday afternoon at Mount Pisgah, West Philadelphia (interesting Sunday-school, warm-hearted congregation); at night at Zion Mission Church, Brother Winder's charge. Also Norristown and Deep Valley (Friday Sept 16), and the N.J. circuits Sept 25-30.

events.name: Organization of the Grand Council of Pennsylvania, I.O. of G.S. and D. of S.
events.location: Philadelphia (affirmed at Wilmington, Del., Sept. 22, 1864)
events.description: Convention of June 20, 1864 recommended a Grand Council for Pennsylvania; lodges represented: Van Brakle D. of S.; National Constitution I.O.G.S.; Grand Council D. of S.; Heart and Hand D. of S.; Moses Biddle I.O.G.S.; Susquehanna Union. Officers elected Sept 4, 1864: R.W.P.G.C. Peter P. Brown; R.W.G. Chief Samuel Van Brakle; R.W.V. Chief Theodore Valentine; R.W.G. Sec. Robert B. J. Procter; R.W.G. Treas. Willis Johnson; R.W.G. Orator James Carroll; R.W.G. Prelate Rev. William Sanford; R.W.G. Conductor Aaron Hopkins. Affirmed by the R.W.N.G. Council at Wilmington, Sept 22. At the national session (Wilmington, Sept 20-24): R.W.N.G. Deputy Chief Samuel Van Brakle (printed 'Ven ...ble') of Pennsylvania; R.W.N.G. Cor. Sec. Robert B. J. Procter of Pennsylvania; Grand L.H.S. to N.G.C. Anna M. Teeple [VERIFY] of Pennsylvania; other officers from Maryland, Ohio, New York, Delaware, N.J. (text only: John H. Anthony, Levin Brown, William H. Wood, Isaac Peck, Jonathan Hamilton, John H. Brice, J. G. Walker, L. H. Wheeler, Spencer Greenwood, James Brister, Keziah Thompson, Mary A. Jackson, Amelia S. Carty). Eulogies on the late R.W.N.G. Chief Edward M. Thomas by Van Brakle and Procter; silver goblets presented to Van Brakle by Hand in Hand Lodge of Wilmington.

events.name: Soldiers' Circle Society of Bethel: hospital visits, Camp William Penn and Summit House
events.location: Camp William Penn hospital; Summit House Hospital
events.description: Society formed in response to the 55th Massachusetts' call (Camp Meigs, Readville, July 15, 1863; acknowledged in the Anglo-African Oct 18, 1863). Committee: Mrs. Sarah Scott, Mrs. Harriet Bacon, Mrs. Mary A. Campbell, Mrs. Jane L. Johnson (President), Miss Esther Armstrong (Secretary). Visits to the hospital at Camp Wm. Penn (first; second March 22, 1864; third June 20, 1864) and to Summit House Hospital (April 25, Aug 27 and Sept 21, 1864), itemizing supplies. Seventh street; Maurice Hall, 1034 Lombard street; Mrs. Sarah Scott, 903 South Ninth street; Mrs. Mary A. Campbell, 832 Carpenter street; Mrs. Jane L. Johnson, 618 South Eighth street; Miss Esther Armstrong, 703 Schriver [VERIFY] street.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference -- first examination of candidates for the itinerancy and elders' orders
events.location: Bethel Church, Sixth St., Philadelphia
events.description: First examination of the Conference year for candidates for the itinerancy and for elders' orders of the Philadelphia Annual Conference, A.M.E. Church, called for Tuesday the 22d instant at 2 1/2 o'clock P.M. Committee: Rev. Wm. Moore, Chairman; Rev. Joseph H. Smith and A. L. Stanford, Secretaries.

events.location: Mission school-house, St. Mary's St. below 7th, Philadelphia
events.description: Standing notice: public temperance meetings every Wednesday at 7 1/2 o'clock 'for the elevation of the colored population'; several good speakers promised. No officers named.

events.location: Preacher's study, Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Special meeting of the Book Committee called by Elisha Weaver, Editor and General Book Steward, for Thursday Nov. 17, 1864, 2 o'clock. Members not named.

events.name: Elisha Weaver preaches on 'The Sabbath Day' at Bethel
events.location: Bethel A.M.E. Church, Sixth Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Sunday evening sermon by Rev. Elisha Weaver, editor of the Christian Recorder, on the Sabbath (text Exodus 20:8), reported by a correspondent signing 'J. C., Phila.' events.description: The quarterly meeting of D. Grand Lodge No. 2, I.O. of G.S. & D. of S., will be held at the new Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street, Philadelphia, on Tuesday, December 6th, 1864, at ten o'clock A.M. events.name: Citizens' meeting in Bethel A.M.E. Church for the Christian Recorder
events.location: Bethel A.M.E. Church, Philadelphia
events.description: A meeting of our citizens was held on Thursday evening, 24th inst. [Nov. 24], to raise subscribers and solicit donations on behalf of the Christian Recorder. Organized with Rev. W. Moore as President, Rev. H. Davis as Vice President, and A. Fields and Thomas H. Boling as Secretaries. The editor [Weaver] spoke on the commencement, progress and present condition of the paper. Dr. Armstrong, 'a well-known and tried friend of the people of color', read passages from a paper he had prepared. After the choir sang, J. M. Langston, the lawyer of Oberlin, spoke extempore ('the three things mostly needed by colored men in this land are, first, money; second, cultivation of intellect; third, political power') and thanked Rev. E. Weaver for defending him from an attack by Rev. Newman in the Colored Citizen. A collection of $82.50 was raised, contributions from $5 to 5 cents. Signed Secs. of Meeting.

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church (Coates St.) -- Thanksgiving sermon and annual Sabbath School exhibition
events.location: Union A.M.E. Church, Coates street, Philadelphia
events.description: Thanksgiving Day: at 3 P.M. the pastor [A. L. Stanford] preached on 'Causes of gratitude to God' (Exodus 15:1-2), heads including the abolition of slavery, the defeat of General McClellan and the peace party of the Chicago platform, and the re-election of President Lincoln. At 8 o'clock the annual exhibition of the Sabbath School, conducted by Professor A. Burris, superintendent; hundreds turned away. A silver cup or goblet was presented to Mr. Isaiah Wears, ex-superintendent, by Miss Mary Louisa Davis on behalf of the school; an original essay by Miss Mary Wears (daughter of Mr. Wears); music by Miss ---- Burris (daughter of Mr. Burris). Stanford proposed a repeat of the exhibition for the benefit of the Recorder and Wilberforce University and to send the paper to soldiers from the vicinity of Union Church, and set the night service of New Year's Day for the benefit of the Recorder.

events.name: Reception for John M. Langston, President of the National Equal Rights' League
events.location: Philadelphia (hall not named)
events.description: Headed 'National Equal Rights' League, Philadelphia, Nov. 2[5 or 8]th, 1864.' A meeting of the colored citizens of Philadelphia, to give a reception to John M. Langston, President of the National Equal Rights' League, was lately held. Organized by the appointment of Rev. Wm. Moore as President. Vice Presidents: Revs. J. C. Gibbs, E. Weaver, Stephen Smith, Wm. J. Alston, James Needham, J. McCrummill, D. B. Bowser, Wm. Whipper and Franklin Turner. Secretaries: J. C. White, Jr., C. R. Cully and D. D. Turner. Langston was introduced by Rev. J. C. Gibbs, who said the public, in connection with the State E. R. League, were assembled to greet the President of the National League. Langston contrasted the laws of Ohio and Pennsylvania, cited the Illinois black law and Attorney-General Bates's opinion on citizenship, Crispus Attucks, and a letter of General Hunter to Governor Tod praising colored troops, and urged united effort through the State organizations. A collection was taken. Resolutions offered by Sergeant-Major Green and unanimously adopted (praising Langston and pledging that 'Philadelphia shall never be found wanting' in support of the movement and of the State Equal Rights' League). Addressed afterward by Rev. J. C. Gibbs, L. H. Putnam of New York, and Rev. Wm. Moore.

events.name: Philadelphia Institute -- supper of the Clayton Aurem Society
events.location: Philadelphia Institute
events.description: A grand supper was served up in style at the Philadelphia Institute, on Wednesday evening, 30th ult., under the auspices of the Clayton Aurem Society. The editor was present until a pretty late hour. After the supper several addresses were delivered; they were very interesting. No names given.

events.name: Meeting at Bethel Church for Wilberforce University (Prof. John G. Mitchell)
events.location: Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Professor John G. Mitchell, of Wilberforce University, has been in our city for several days, collecting contributions and maturing plans for the ladies to work. 'We gave him a chance to speak of Wilberforce before a portion of our citizens, and on last Tuesday evening we gave him a meeting at Bethel Church.' The audience was smaller than wished. He left on Thursday for Baltimore. (Mitchell is from Ohio; not linked.)

events.name: Celebration of the Emancipation in Maryland (Colored Union League), National Hall
events.location: National Hall, Market St., Philadelphia
events.description: On Wednesday evening, the 7th inst., a large portion of our colored citizens assembled in National Hall, Market St., to celebrate the freeing of nearly one hundred thousand men, women and children in Maryland. The Colored Union League of our city gave notice through the weekly and daily papers. The choirs of the churches were invited; over one hundred voices. Programme: music by the orchestra; prayer by Rev. J. B. Trusty; grand anthem 'O give thanks' by the choir; Emancipation song composed by A. W. Lively; remarks by the president, J. C. Bowers; anthem 'The Lord is King'; speech by Sergt. Major A. M. Green; anthem 'My weary spirit'; speech by Rev. W. J. Alston; Star-Spangled Banner; remarks by Mr. Lowe [?]; trio sung by Messrs. Cliff, Sturgis and Dangerfield; anthem; address by Rev. Theo. D. Miller; song 'Viva L'America' by T. J. Bowers; resolutions read by Prof. Green and adopted; 'Mother, when the war is over' by A. W. Lively and others; closing address by Major Morgan, 43d U.S.C.T. Rev. J. C. Gibbs gave way to Major Morgan. Recalls that the first vessel captured by the rebels from the North was recaptured by a colored man, and the steamer Planter taken by Capt. Robert Small[s]. Orchestra under Mr. F. V. Seymour; Mr. Lively arranged the choir and chorus.

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League -- call for State Convention at Harrisburg
events.location: Harrisburg, Pa.
events.description: Call: A Convention will be held in Harrisburg on the second Wednesday in February, 1865 [Feb. 8], at 10 o'clock A.M., in accordance with the order of the National Convention held at Syracuse, New York, Oct. 4, 1864 [printed 1861]. Basis of representation: ten dollars for the first and five dollars for each additional representative from each Equal Rights League, Church, Lodge or any other existing association. 'Come from your mountain homes, come from your valleys, and organize for united action. The franchise, the interest of the colored soldier, the means and manner of education in our State, demand our earnest and undivided efforts.' Signed Jonathan C. Gibbs, Jacob C. White, Jr., Sergt. Alfred M. Green. By order of the State Equal Rights League.

events.name: Banneker Institute -- second anniversary of the Emancipation Proclamation (announced)
events.location: National Hall, Market street above 12th, Philadelphia
events.description: 'Proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof.' The second anniversary of the Emancipation Proclamation will be celebrated, under the auspices of the Banneker Institute, on Monday evening, January 2d, 1865, in National Hall, Market street, above 12th. Music by the United States Military Post Band, from Camp William Penn, and by several gentlemen of the musical profession, prominent among whom are Messrs. Bowers, Cliff and Lively. events.location: Concert Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: The Executive Committee of the Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the colored people of Pennsylvania have, for some time past, been preparing for a course of lectures, to be held in Concert Hall, this winter. The Hall has been secured, also the following speakers engaged: Wm. Lloyd Garrison, Fred. Douglass, Rev. Sella Martin, J. M. Langston, Esq., Hon. W. D. Kelley, and Mrs. F. E. W. Harper.
